dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts hardrock mining operators, federal land management agencies, and communities near abandoned hardrock mines.
dimensions.evidence: allows mining operators to use federal lands for activities ancillary to mining, such as waste disposal

dimensions.assessment: Addresses court decisions by explicitly permitting multiple mill site claims for waste disposal and creates a dedicated funding mechanism for abandoned mine reclamation.
dimensions.evidence: establish the Abandoned Hardrock Mine Fund, and for other purposes

dimensions.assessment: Directs claim maintenance fees collected on mill sites into a newly established fund for abandoned mine reclamation, to be spent without further appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: Any amounts collected... on mill sites... shall be deposited into the Fund... without further appropriations, only to carry out section 40704

dimensions.assessment: Amends federal mining laws and the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993 to add provisions for multiple mill sites and establish a Treasury fund.
dimensions.evidence: Section 2337 of the Revised Statutes (30 U.S.C. 42) is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory changes to hardrock mining law and long-term establishment of the reclamation fund.
dimensions.evidence: There is established in the Treasury of the United States a separate account, to be known as the Abandoned Hardrock Mine Fund

missing_information: Projections of the annual revenue generated from mill site claim maintenance fees to be deposited into the fund are not provided.
importance_detail.rationale: Allows mining operators on federal lands to locate multiple mill site claims reasonably necessary for operations regardless of mineral deposit validity, and establishes the Abandoned Hardrock Mine Fund funded by mill site claim maintenance fees.

card.summary: H.R. 4754, the Department of the Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026, provides federal funding and sets policy guidelines for fiscal year 2026 for the Department of the Interior, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the U.S. Forest Service, the Indian Health Service, and various related cultural and historical agencies.
